summary: Full-stack testing of GiroExpress (FastAPI+Mongo+React). Backend: created pytest suite (48 tests) covering health, auth/JWT/cookies/bcrypt, pricing table+quote (km & geocoding), delivery CRUD + RBAC, 3-simultaneous-per-store batch limit, courier approve/online/accept/start/complete, weekly statement accumulation, proof upload to object storage + /api/files RBAC, admin statement approval, chat, tickets, admin users/block/stats/bank settings. Result 47/48 passing (only missing brute-force lockout). Frontend: Playwright e2e on public URL — admin login->/admin, store register->/loja, delivery creation (manual slider 3km => R$5,99/R$4,99/19min and auto geocoding via OSM), courier register->pending banner + blocked online toggle, admin approve via UI, courier online->accept->complete, statement auto-created and proof upload (status COMPROVANTE ENVIADO), admin approve statement + resolve ticket, chat send/receive, ticket creation, route RBAC redirects (store->/admin->/loja, courier->/loja->/motoboy, admin->/loja->/admin). One real 500 bug found and fixed (ObjectId leaked in chat POST response).

minor.issue: No brute-force protection / account lockout / rate limiting: 6+ consecutive wrong passwords all return 401 with no throttling (playbook requires lockout after 5 failed attempts)

Couriers with status='pending' (not yet approved) can list all available deliveries including store pickup and client dropoff addresses/phones. Accept is blocked, but data exposure to unapproved accounts should be gated by status=='active'
Batch limit check counts ALL deliveries with the batch_id regardless of status, and allow_batch is validated only when a batch_id is given; also no validation that batch_id belongs to the store
status is a free-form string (no enum validation); admin can set any arbitrary status value. Also ObjectId(user_id) is unvalidated -> 500 on malformed id
ObjectId(delivery_id) not wrapped in try/except (unlike GET) -> malformed id raises 500 instead of 400
Statement stays 'open' forever if not paid; no auto-closure/overdue logic on due_date (Tuesday) — may be out of scope but no scheduled job exists

ui_bugs.issue: Modal cannot be closed with Escape key or backdrop click (only the X button); while open its full-screen overlay intercepts all clicks on the dashboard
Missing data-testid on subject input, priority select, description textarea and submit button — had to fall back to placeholder/text selectors

The 'Calcular distância automaticamente' checkbox had no data-testid; added data-testid="auto-calc-toggle" (test-only change). Distance slider only exists when auto-calc is off — expected, documented for next agent

issues: Uses native browser <select> for 'Prioridade' instead of the shadcn Select component, inconsistent with the rest of the dark UI
Logo image renders as a small dark square badge with very low contrast against the dark header; brand wordmark 'GiroExpress' is not shown in dashboards (only on login)

action_items: Add brute-force protection to POST /api/auth/login (failed-attempt counter + temporary lockout returning 423/429) as required by the auth playbook
Gate available-deliveries listing (and its addresses/phones) for couriers with status != 'active'
Wrap ObjectId(...) conversions in accept/start/complete/cancel/chat/tickets/admin endpoints to return 400 instead of 500 for malformed ids
Validate admin user status against an enum ('active','pending','blocked')
Add data-testid to TicketModal fields/submit and allow closing ChatModal via Escape/backdrop
Consider replacing the native priority <select> with the shadcn Select for visual consistency
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED by tester: POST /api/deliveries/{id}/chat returned 500 because insert_one mutated the dict adding ObjectId _id which was then spread into the JSON response ('ObjectId' object is not iterable). Now excludes _id.
server.py is ~780 lines and mixes auth, pricing, deliveries, statements, storage, tickets and admin — split into routers/services modules.
Storage helpers (init_storage/put_object/get_object) and geocode_address use blocking `requests` inside async endpoints — this blocks the event loop; use httpx.AsyncClient or run_in_threadpool.
storage_key is a module-level global mutated without a lock; concurrent uploads can race on re-init.
current_cycle_bounds uses UTC only; a Brazilian (UTC-3) Sunday->Saturday cycle will roll over 3h early — consider America/Sao_Paulo tz.
accumulate_statement pushes delivery_ids without idempotency guard; a repeated complete call path (or future retry) could double-count totals.
seed_data_creation: API test users prefixed TEST_ (auto-cleaned by session fixture). UI test users left in DB for reuse: uitest_store_1786044393@example.com / Secret@123 (store, has delivered order + approved statement) and uitest_courier_1786044475@example.com / Secret@123 (courier, approved+online). Several older test_* users from the first failing run remain in DB and appear in the admin list.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run backend suite serially: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/backend_test.py -n 0` (tests share a module-level STATE dict, so xdist loadscope splits break them). Only test_brute_force_lockout fails — feature not implemented. Frontend: new-delivery modal defaults to auto geocoding (Nominatim works from this env, ~10km for vague addresses); uncheck [data-testid='auto-calc-toggle'] to reveal [data-testid='distance-slider']. Statement for the UI store is already APPROVED, so re-upload of proof is blocked there — create a fresh store for upload retests. Old test_* users clutter the admin list; consider purging DB before UI screenshots.
rca_of_the_issue: Chat 500: send_chat spread the inserted document into the response, and motor's insert_one mutates the passed dict by injecting the ObjectId `_id`, which FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize (TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable). Fixed by filtering out `_id` when building the response; re-ran chat tests (backend + UI) and both pass.
